title: What Documents Does a Section 13B Divorce Petition Need?
desc: A section 13B mutual divorce petition at the Family Court, Haldwani, needs proof of marriage, address proof, one year's separation, and a signed settlement.
why: Couples who have already agreed to separate often delay filing simply because they are unsure what papers the Family Court will ask for.
keyPoints: A joint petition under section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 needs proof of marriage, proof of one year's separate living, and address proof for both spouses.
A written settlement covering alimony, return of stridhan, and custody of children is essential, even though the law does not fix its format.
At Haldwani's Family Court, both spouses must appear and sign the joint statement before the court registers the petition.
Missing or inconsistent documents are a common reason hearings get adjourned, adding months to an otherwise quick process.

sections.h: What documents does a section 13B petition need?
p: A section 13B mutual consent divorce petition filed at the Family Court, Haldwani, needs five basic documents: proof of marriage, proof that both spouses lived separately for at least one year, address proof for each spouse, recent photographs, and a signed settlement covering money and children. Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 itself does not list documents, but courts ask for these to confirm the facts the petition must prove.

If no marriage certificate exists, courts usually accept other proof, such as wedding photographs, the invitation card, or a priest's certificate, along with both spouses' affidavits confirming the marriage.

sections.h: What should the settlement paper cover?
p: The settlement (often called a memorandum of understanding) should spell out the amount and mode of alimony, if any; return of stridhan (the wife's personal gifts and jewellery); custody, visitation and maintenance of any children; and confirmation that neither spouse has other pending cases against the other, or that those cases will be withdrawn.
This paper is attached to the petition and read out before the court records each spouse's statement on oath at the first motion.

sections.h: What happens after the papers are filed?
p: After the first motion, the law allows the second motion only between six and eighteen months later, though the Supreme Court held in Amardeep Singh v. Harveen Kaur (2017) that this gap can be waived if the couple has been separated well over a year and has already settled everything. At the second motion, both spouses confirm their consent again, and the court passes the divorce decree.

whatToDo: Collect your marriage certificate; if you do not have one, gather wedding photographs or the invitation card instead.
Put the full settlement in writing and have both spouses sign it before the first motion.
Carry Aadhaar or another address proof, passport-size photographs, and children's birth certificates if applicable.
Check your hearing dates and orders on the eCourts portal using your case number.

hi.title: धारा 13बी के तलाक़ याचिका में कौन-कौन से कागज़ चाहिए?
keyPoints: हिंदू विवाह अधिनियम, 1955 की धारा 13बी के तहत संयुक्त याचिका के लिए विवाह का प्रमाण, एक वर्ष अलग रहने का प्रमाण और दोनों पक्षों का पता-प्रमाण चाहिए।
गुज़ारा भत्ता, स्त्रीधन की वापसी और बच्चों की अभिरक्षा तय करने वाला लिखित समझौता भी ज़रूरी है।
हल्द्वानी के परिवार न्यायालय में दोनों पक्षों को स्वयं उपस्थित होकर संयुक्त बयान पर हस्ताक्षर करने होते हैं।
कागज़ात अधूरे या असंगत होने से सुनवाई टलती है, जिससे प्रक्रिया में महीनों की देरी होती है।
p: यदि विवाह प्रमाण-पत्र नहीं है, तो न्यायालय आमतौर पर शादी की तस्वीरें, निमंत्रण पत्र या पंडित का प्रमाण-पत्र भी स्वीकार कर लेते हैं, साथ में दोनों पक्षों का हलफ़नामा।

sources.title: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, section 13B (India Code)
Amardeep Singh v. Harveen Kaur, Supreme Court of India, 12 September 2017
